newsitem.title: USA: AMR Corp Q1 fuel costs, oper expenses rise.
newsitem.headline: AMR Corp Q1 fuel costs, oper expenses rise.

text.p: AMR Corp on Wednesday posted a decline in first-quarter profit after three months that brought labor unrest, higher fuel costs and increased operating expenses to its American Airlines unit.
AMR's first-quarter earnings fell to $1.65 per diluted share from $1.84 in the same period of 1996. Its total operating revenues rose to $4.4 billion from $4.3 billion.

The current first-quarter results included a $20 million charge for stock options awarded to its pilots as part of a tentative wage settlement reached two weeks ago after months of bitter negotiations.

"Despite the effects of a threatened pilot strike, strong levels of demand, combined with relatively limited capacity additions, produced good results for us," AMR chairman Robert Crandall said in a statement.
"While our results are testimony to the continuing strength of demand, they would have been dramatically better absent the labor dispute," Crandall said.

AMR said American's fuel costs increased 16.9 percent to $0.747 a gallon, compared with $0.639 per gallon in the year-earlier period. AMR's total aircraft fuel expenses rose to $520 million from $441 million last year.
American's operating expenses rose 4.8 percent to $0.0940 per available seat mile from $0.0897 per available seat. AMR's total operating expenses rose to $3.7 billion from $3.6 billion.
American's first-quarter passenger load factor was 67.4 percent, compared to 65.6 percent last year.
